case_number: Criminal Appeal No. of 2022 (Arising out of Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No. of 2022, Arising out of Diary No. 21596/2020)
summary: The State of Rajasthan appealed against the Rajasthan High Court's decision to reduce Banwari Lal's sentence under Section 307 IPC from three years rigorous imprisonment to the period already undergone (44 days), while upholding his conviction. The High Court did not provide detailed reasoning or consider the gravity of the offence, nature of injuries (lacerated wound to the skull penetrating the brain membrane), or relevant sentencing principles. The Supreme Court found the High Court's approach casual and unsustainable, emphasizing that sentencing must consider aggravating and mitigating factors. The delay of 1880 days in filing the appeal was condoned given the seriousness of the issue.
legal_provisions_cited: State of Rajasthan v. Mohan Lal, (2018) 18 SCC 535
State of Madhya Pradesh v. Udham, (2019) 10 SCC 300
Satish Kumar Jayanti Lal Dabgar v. State of Gujarat, (2015) 7 SCC 359
final_judgment: Appeal allowed; impugned judgment of the High Court quashed; sentence of three years rigorous imprisonment imposed by the trial court restored for Banwari Lal. Benefit of probation for Mohan Lal remains undisturbed.
